metadata.title: Notable cyber individuals (public-record figures) - wired to their groups/events
metadata.frame: A first, tightly-scoped set of NAMED individuals from the cyber-history corpus who are unambiguously public (indictments, sanctions, memoirs, major press) and warrant a strategic-behavior dossier. Each is a person node linked to the org/event they are known for. Companion dossiers live in the Persons tab; this block only wires the graph edges.
metadata.grade: Roles, convictions, sanctions, and signature events = FACT (DOJ/OFAC/court records; on-record interviews). Any behavioral assessment is in the Persons dossier, labeled inference with calibrated confidence - not fact.
metadata.honest_limits: Public-record ROLE only here - no private/biographical detail, no home/family/location data (no doxxing). Inclusion = materially documented in the corpus, NOT an accusation beyond what courts/sanctions already state. Living people; excluded from the formal proofs.
metadata.method: DOJ/SDNY + OFAC records; court filings; on-record interviews + memoirs. Dossiers follow the Persons-tab leadership-analysis method (BLUF/drivers/worldview/etc., graded).

edges.notes: Assange founded WikiLeaks (2006) and was its editor/public face through the 2010 megaleaks; extradition fight ended 2024 with a US plea deal (time served) freeing him to Australia (fact).
edges.source: #241 individuals (public record; US v. Assange plea 2024)

edges.notes: Snowden (NSA contractor, Booz Allen) leaked the 2013 mass-surveillance archive (PRISM, upstream/backbone collection, XKeyscore) to journalists - the disclosure that reshaped the global privacy/PQC debate (fact).

Stranded in Moscow in 2013 (US revoked his passport en route); granted asylum, then Russian citizenship (2022). His location is a matter of geopolitics, not endorsement - noted as jurisdictional fact.

Yakubets is the accused leader of Evil Corp (Dridex/Zeus lineage); OFAC-sanctioned + DOJ-indicted (2019), with a $5M reward and reported FSB links; 2024 UK/US actions named further associates + a LockBit tie (fact/attribution).
Hutchins (MalwareTech) registered the kill-switch domain that stopped WannaCry's spread (May-2017) - the accidental-hero moment of the outbreak (fact).

Months later the DOJ arrested Hutchins over his earlier authorship of the Kronos banking trojan; he pleaded guilty (2019) and received time served + supervised release - a redemption/ambiguity arc (researcher and, earlier, malware author) (fact).
